# Special profile transitioned to by unconfined when creating an unprivileged
# user namespace.
#
abi <abi/4.0>,
include <tunables/global>

profile unprivileged_userns {
     audit deny capability,
     audit deny change_profile,

     # allow block to be replaced by allow when x dominance test is fixed
     #allow all,
     allow network,
     allow signal,
     allow dbus,
     allow file rwlkm /**,
     allow unix,
     allow mqueue,
     allow ptrace,
     allow userns,

     # stack children to strip capabilities
     allow pix /** -> &unprivileged_userns ,

     # Site-specific additions and overrides. See local/README for details.
     include if exists <local/unprivileged_userns>
}

# This profile allows almost everything and only exists to allow
# bwrap to work on a system with user namespace restrictions
# being enforced.
# bwrap is allowed access to user namespaces and capabilities
# within the user namespace, but its children do not have
# capabilities, blocking bwrap from being able to be used to
# arbitrarily by-pass the user namespace restrictions.
#
# Note: the bwrap child is stacked against the bwrap profile due to
# bwraps use of no-new-privs

# disabled by default as it can break some use cases on a system that
# doesn't have or has disable user namespace restrictions for unconfined
# use aa-enforce to enable it

abi <abi/4.0>,

include <tunables/global>

profile bwrap /usr/bin/bwrap flags=(attach_disconnected) {
  allow capability,
  # not allow all, to allow for pix stack
  # sadly we have to allow  m every where to allow children to work under
  # stacking.
  allow file rwlkm /{**,},
  allow network,
  allow unix,
  allow ptrace,
  allow signal,
  allow mqueue,
  allow io_uring,
  allow userns,
  allow mount,
  allow umount,
  allow pivot_root,
  allow dbus,
  allow px /** -> bwrap//&unpriv_bwrap,

  # the local include should not be used without understanding the userns
  # restriction.
  # Site-specific additions and overrides. See local/README for details.
  include if exists <local/bwrap-userns-restrict>
}

profile unpriv_bwrap flags=(attach_disconnected) {
  # not allow all, to allow for pix stack
  allow file rwlkm /{**,},
  allow network,
  allow unix,
  allow ptrace,
  allow signal,
  allow mqueue,
  allow io_uring,
  allow userns,
  allow mount,
  allow umount,
  allow pivot_root,
  allow dbus,

  allow pix /** -> &unpriv_bwrap,

  audit deny capability,

  # the local include should not be used without understanding the userns
  # restriction.
  # Site-specific additions and overrides. See local/README for details.
  include if exists <local/unpriv_bwrap>
}

causal_findings.finding: The original 'Failed to make / slave' denial is caused by the outer docker-default AppArmor profile.
causal_findings.confidence: confirmed by controlled A/B behavior and pinned Moby source
evidence: Matrix B removes only docker-default and advances
Moby template explicitly says deny mount

causal_findings.finding: Using apparmor=unconfined is not a solution on this Ubuntu host.
evidence: Host /etc/apparmor.d/unprivileged_userns states that unconfined tasks transition to it
That profile contains audit deny capability
Matrix B fails when bwrap uses RTM_NEWADDR, which requires namespace-local network capability

causal_findings.finding: The host lacks the Ubuntu bwrap-userns-restrict profile recommended by official OpenAI documentation.
evidence: Both documented profile locations are missing
apparmor-profiles and apparmor-utils are not installed
Offline package inspection shows the missing profile permits bwrap userns, mount, pivot_root and capabilities while denying capabilities to children

causal_findings.finding: The upstream Ubuntu profile cannot be used byte-for-byte with the current image path.

remediation_design_not_applied.preferred: Keep the fixed bwrap binary and all container isolation. Draft a task-scoped AppArmor policy based on Ubuntu's bwrap-userns-restrict semantics, adapted to /opt/agent/bin/bwrap, and a constrained parent container profile that explicitly transitions only that executable into the bwrap profile. Load it on the host only after separate review/approval, then rerun the full 06p positive and negative tests.
remediation_design_not_applied.alternative: Move the fixed binary to /usr/bin/bwrap in a rebuilt candidate image and still provide a safe transition from the container parent profile; the stock profile alone does not automatically prove a transition from docker-default.
remediation_design_not_applied.note: No AppArmor profile was drafted, installed, loaded or attached by this diagnostic step.
